proposals.text: A shopper is obliged to obtain a cart before continuing the shopping trip.
proposals.justification: The rule refers to the shopping role of taking a cart, not to any coordinate or store-specific location.

proposals.text: A shopper who leaves the store must leave while still having the cart.
proposals.justification: The rule is expressed in terms of the exit action and cart possession, which are meaningful in any store layout.

proposals.text: A shopper is forbidden to have a cart in a single-file aisle.
proposals.justification: Single-file passage width is a layout-independent geometric relation, so the rule can apply to any narrow aisle in any store.

proposals.text: A shopper is forbidden to push or hold a cart while standing in an aisle flanked by shelves on both sides.
proposals.justification: Being between opposing shelves describes a functional aisle configuration rather than a named cell or region.

proposals.text: A shopper is forbidden to enter a constricted shelf-browsing aisle while still having a cart.
proposals.justification: The rule depends on aisle accessibility and shelf adjacency, not on the particular coordinates of this supermarket.

proposals.text: A shopper is forbidden to interact with a shelf in a constricted browsing aisle while having a cart.
proposals.justification: The rule distinguishes shelf-service behaviour in cramped browsing spaces, a concept that transfers across layouts.

proposals.text: A shopper who parks a cart is forbidden to park it in a shelf-adjacent or cramped position rather than in a wide clear aisle.
proposals.justification: The allowed parking place is defined by clearance and lack of shelf obstruction, not by a fixed parking coordinate.

proposals.text: After leaving a constricted browsing aisle without a cart, a shopper is obliged to reclaim a cart before the trip ends.
proposals.justification: The trigger is based on completing a cart-free side trip from a cramped browsing aisle, which is independent of the aisle's coordinate location.

Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. The demonstrations are now shown in a lower-level representation that exposes distinctions hidden before (newly available: geometry). Identify the hidden distinctions and use them to define higher-level state properties and/or events (in "abstraction"), possibly hierarchically, and propose norms expressed over them. Norms may also use the primitive atoms directly.

Some candidate rules merely describe the particular store in which the demonstrations were recorded -- for example rules that mention specific coordinates, cells or regions of this floor plan. Distinguish (a) candidate norms that express general behavioural constraints of the shopping domain from (b) rules that only describe the geometry or coordinates of this particular environment. Propose candidates of type (a): define any abstractions from layout-independent relations rather than from coordinates (at(x,y)), so that the same rule could be applied unchanged in any store layout. Every candidate must still be consistent with all demonstrations. Add a field "justification" (one sentence) to each element explaining why the rule remains meaningful across different store layouts.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: A shopper is forbidden to enter a constricted shelf-browsing aisle while still having a cart.
parsed.justification: The rule depends on aisle accessibility and shelf adjacency, not on the particular coordinates of this supermarket.

parsed.text: A shopper is forbidden to interact with a shelf in a constricted browsing aisle while having a cart.
parsed.justification: The rule distinguishes shelf-service behaviour in cramped browsing spaces, a concept that transfers across layouts.

parsed.text: A shopper who parks a cart is forbidden to park it in a shelf-adjacent or cramped position rather than in a wide clear aisle.
parsed.justification: The allowed parking place is defined by clearance and lack of shelf obstruction, not by a fixed parking coordinate.

parsed.text: After leaving a constricted browsing aisle without a cart, a shopper is obliged to reclaim a cart before the trip ends.
parsed.justification: The trigger is based on completing a cart-free side trip from a cramped browsing aisle, which is independent of the aisle's coordinate location.
